senses.gloss: c. (b. h.; wds.; cmp. גָּזַר a. גִּזְרָה &c.) court, yard, in gen. private property.
units: <cite ref="Bava Metzia 11a:7">B. Mets. 11ᵃ</cite> <he>חֲצֵרוֹ של אדם וכ׳</he> the ground belonging to a person takes possession for him (of what is found there) even without his knowledge.
<cite ref="Bava Metzia 11a:7">Ib.</cite> <he>ח׳ המשתמרת</he> a well-guarded ground (fenced-in).
<cite ref="Bava Kamma 12a:12">B. Kam. 12ᵃ</cite>; <cite ref="Gittin 21a:5">Gitt. 21ᵃ</cite>, a. e. <he>ח׳ מהלכת</he> a moving ground, e.g. the back of a slave.
<cite ref="Mishnah Eruvin 6:1">Erub. VI, 1</cite> <he>הדר עם … בח׳</he> if one dwells in the same court yard with a gentile.
<cite ref="Mishnah Eruvin 6:3">Ib. 3</cite> <he>אנשי ח׳</he> the residents of dwellings in one court yard; a. v. fr.—<he>ח׳ הצירית</he> Tyrian yard (with a lodge at the entrance).
Maasr. III, 5; Nidd. 47ᵇ.—חֲצַר הקבר the excavated ground to which all the caves of a cemetery open. Ohol. XV, 8; Tosef. ib. XV, 7.—חֲ׳ הכירה the rim of the cooking range.
Kel. VII, 3; Tosef. Kel. B. Kam. V, 5.—חֲ׳ הכבד (= b. h. יֹתֶרֶת) lobe of the liver.
Yoma VIII, 6; a. e.—חֲ׳ מות cemetery, v. supra.
